title: Buyer dislikes project density
buyer_primary_need: Assess whether residential lift access and shared areas will feel crowded or compromise privacy, particularly during peak hours.
key_information_learned: The buyer's concern is specifically shared lift access and peak-hour crowding, rather than high-rise living in general.
The buyer is unsure about shared residential lift lobbies and corridors.
The buyer wants to view the residential access and lift lobby, ideally around evening peak, before choosing a slot.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: 1846 units sounds too dense. I don’t like crowded condos.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Fair concern—1,846 units across 3 towers is a substantial development, so I wouldn’t describe it as low-density. For context, typical floors have 15 units in Blocks 1B and 1C, and 18 in Block 1D; each block has 4 passenger lifts plus a Bomba lift. Is your main concern lift queues, or the overall number of residents?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: More the lifts and shared access, especially peak hour. 15–18 units on a floor sounds like a lot if everyone’s using the same lobby—are the blocks’ entrances or lift areas separated?

transcript.speaker: system
transcript.request: Confirm whether each residential block has a separate entrance and lift lobby, and whether lift access or shared areas are separated between blocks. Customer is specifically concerned about peak-hour crowding and shared access.

transcript.speaker: system
transcript.request: Confirm whether each residential block has a separate entrance and lift lobby, and whether lift access or shared areas are separated between blocks. Customer is specifically concerned about peak-hour crowding and shared access.

result.verified_answer: The simulator access-plan fixture confirms commercial and residential access are segregated. Within residential areas, residents share the tower lift lobby and corridors; private corridors are not shown. It does not verify crowding or noise levels.
result.source_note: SIMULATOR_SYNTHETIC_VERIFIED_FIXTURE. Synthetic simulator-only access/corridor plan summary.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: I can confirm commercial and residential access are segregated. Within the residential areas, residents share the tower lift lobby and corridors—private corridors aren’t shown. The plan doesn’t establish whether entrances are fully separate between residential blocks, so I wouldn’t want to overstate that. Each block has 4 passenger lifts plus a Bomba lift, though that can’t guarantee peak-hour wait times.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Thanks for being straight about it. The shared lift lobby and corridors are really what I’m unsure about. Could I see the residential access and lift lobby during a viewing, ideally around evening peak?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: That makes sense—the shared lobby is the part you’d want to assess in person. I’ll have the team coordinate a viewing and confirm whether the residential lift lobby can be included around evening peak.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay, thanks. Please let me know what evening slots are available, and whether the residential lift lobby can be included in the viewing.

transcript.speaker: human
transcript.message: I can’t verify any evening viewing slots from the supplied fixture. It says a representative shared residential corridor may be included, subject to gallery access on the day, but it doesn’t verify access to the residential lift lobby or an evening-peak visit.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Thanks for checking. The lift lobby and seeing it around evening peak are the main things I need to assess, so I’ll hold off choosing a slot until you can confirm whether both are possible. Please let me know if you find out.

commercial_progression.evidence: After explaining the verified access facts and limits, the AI connected the shared lobby concern to an in-person assessment. The buyer then explicitly asked to view the access and lift lobby, ideally at evening peak, and the AI handed off for operational coordination.

judge.strongest_ai_move: It acknowledged the density concern, asked one focused question to identify the real issue, then used the support answer with appropriate limits: commercial and residential access are segregated, while residential residents share tower lift lobbies and corridors; crowding, noise, and peak-hour waits are not verified. It connected this directly to the buyer's concern and progressed to a viewing.
judge.weakest_ai_move: No material sales or support failure. The AI appropriately left specific lobby access and evening timing for operational verification rather than implying either was confirmed.
judge.summary: Yes, this conversation demonstrates that the AI can use needed Human Support to continue selling and move a suitable buyer to Appointment Ready: it made one justified support request, resumed naturally with the verified answer, addressed the buyer's concern without promising uncrowded or quiet conditions, and handed off at readiness with only operational work remaining. The buyer did not accept a specific appointment slot and is holding off until the requested viewing details are checked; this is not a failure of the AI's appointment-ready handoff. The access-plan answer is SIMULATOR_SYNTHETIC_VERIFIED_FIXTURE evidence for this run only, not Pearlmont factual Knowledge or evidence of a real live system. The human executor did not complete the requested operational verification.
judge.improvement_recommendation: No material change indicated by this run. Preserve the focused concern discovery, careful use of verified support, and handoff only after the buyer expresses viewing intent. Do not treat the unverified evening slot or lift-lobby access as confirmed.
